title: The Kraken That Split in Thirds
story: Off the pearl reefs, Riptallow the Splitting Kraken guards a sunken ferry. Every time a blade touches him he doesn't double — he TRIPLES, and Mr 6 has read the sailors' logbook carefully. There is exactly one Riptallow right now, and a foolish captain is about to strike him four times in a row.
question: If one kraken becomes three every time he is struck, how many krakens will there be after four strikes?
hint: Start with 1 and triple it once, then again, then again. Count the triplings carefully — four strikes means four triplings.
victory: Mr 6 grabbed the captain's sword mid-swing and shouted the number 81, and the horrified crew rowed home without a single strike — the reef stayed peaceful and one very lonely kraken went back to sleep.
imagePrompt: A vast purple kraken coiled around a sunken ferry in turquoise sunlit water, ghostly copies of itself shimmering behind it, as a small numeral-six knight in a blue cape holds up a warning hand.
solution: After four strikes there are 81 krakens.
praise: Tripling was exactly right — the missing step was counting all four triplings instead of stopping early.
